newsitem.title: PERU: Peru may award cellphone concession by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Peru may award cellphone concession by year-end.

text.p: Peru's government said late Wednesday it hoped to award by year end a concession for the country's second cellular telephone frequency band in the provinces.

"The plan to offer the provincial B band of cellular telephones is already approved," said Luis Piazzon, government head of telephone concession sales. "We will probably announce the sale to firms in late August.
"We think that the band could be awarded at an auction before the end of 1997."

Awarding the concession would mean Telefonica del Peru losing its monopoly on cellular telephone services in the provinces. The telecom -- controlled by Spain's Telefonica de Espana -- currently owns the only concession for the provinces, known as frequency band A, and is prohibited from bidding on the second band.

Tele 2000 -- Telefonica's only competition for the cellular telephone market in Lima and the neighboring Callao port area -- has said it is keen to win the concession of the provincial B band frequency.
Tele 2000 is so far the only known contender for the B band cellular concession.
Market sources said Tele 2000 -- controlled by U.S. giant BellSouth Corp -- would likely have to offer up to $100 million to win the auction.
